pairs.subject: read-serving-replicas
pairs.evidence: apps/console/src/data/config.ts:5 The console talks to one daemon on loopback (the desktop shell, a query param or env picks a single URL). There is no single-leader service with standby replicas serving reads, which is this subject's precondition. A case-insensitive search of apps/console/src/data for replica, leader, follower, standby, forward and applied found none of them (only TypeScript `readonly`), and the daemon crate has no replica or leader-election concept either.

techniques.evidence: apps/console/src/data/rpc.ts:57 The RPC request carries only method and params, with no echoed position. With one authority and no lagging replica there is no read-your-writes gap for an index to close.

apps/console/src/data/cache.ts:1 This is a client-side query cache, invalidated by pushed daemon events and its own mutations, with a 5-minute TTL backstop. It is not a replica's derivation fed by a committed-write stream, so the hook rule does not govern it.

apps/console/src/data/cache.ts:137 It marks entries stale and refetches rather than writing values in, and aborts an in-flight fill on refetch. But there is no replica apply or concurrency against a log, so the technique's precondition does not hold.
apps/console/src/data/rpc.ts:54 Every call goes to the one daemon base URL. There is no replica that could refuse a write and forward the request.
